$comment: Single source of truth for the community catalog taxonomy. tools/validate.py asserts that schema/manifest.schema.json carries the same enum values, so the two cannot drift.

engineering.label: Engineering
engineering.description: Designs, builds or reviews software and infrastructure.

product.label: Product
product.description: Strategy, discovery, roadmaps, PRDs and launch planning.

project.label: Project
project.description: Delivery planning, coordination, estimation and progress tracking.

quality.label: Quality
quality.description: Testing, acceptance, review and quality assurance workflows.

knowledge.label: Knowledge
knowledge.description: Documents, notes, wikis, information architecture and retrieval.

research.label: Research
research.description: Investigation, literature review, competitive and market analysis.

data.label: Data
data.description: Data analysis, transformation, pipelines and reporting.

writing.label: Writing
writing.description: Drafting, editing, translation and long-form content.

devops.label: DevOps
devops.description: CI/CD, deployment, monitoring and incident response.

design.label: Design
design.description: Design systems, visual assets and design review support.

support.label: Support
support.description: Customer support, triage and service operations.

other.label: Other
other.description: Anything that does not fit the categories above.

core.label: Core
core.description: Single-purpose agent, at most 3 skills, no Shell, Sandbox or out-of-sandbox write permissions.

extended.label: Extended
extended.description: Multi-capability agent, at most 10 skills, may write inside its workspace but never shells out.

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.description: Agent that may execute commands or run outside a sandbox. Requires maintainer review before publishing.

tier_semantics.$comment: tier is a CAPABILITY level, not a trust level. It is derived from the agent's own declarations and is never rendered as an official or verified badge. The values are deliberately disjoint from the main repo's official/community vocabulary.

package_policy.$comment: An agent package contains no binaries. Its capability surface is exactly prompt + skills + tools + mcp; any binary capability is reached through an stdio MCP server that lives outside the package.

mcp_declaration.note: MCP servers are referenced by name only. A package declares the MCP tools it wants; the server binary and its stdio transport configuration are supplied by the runtime, never shipped inside the package.
